capabilities: browser-code-editor | Serves VS Code in a web browser, with a file explorer, extensions from Open VSX and an integrated terminal that runs shell commands inside the container.
description:
UnitySVC runs the official code-server image (VS Code in the browser, from Coder) in a separate container for each enrollment, with its own HTTPS address. You get the VS Code editor in a browser tab: a file explorer, the integrated terminal, extensions from the Open VSX registry, and a workspace folder that is kept in your home. The terminal is a real shell in the container, with git, curl and a passwordless sudo; the container is not privileged, and it is yours alone.

Enroll in the base channel and keep or replace the generated password. Open `https://<instance>/`, enter the password, and the editor opens on the `project` folder. Anyone who knows the password has a full shell in the container, so treat it like a root password. You can run one instance at a time. See How to use this service for full setup, what is kept and what is lost.

You pay the selected channel's platform compute cost while the instance runs, including idle time. Only the `project` folder is stored; settings, extensions and installed tools are lost when the instance stops. Labs adds no markup and receives no seller payout. See the code-server documentation and issue tracker for software-specific help.
